display: Former senior colour matcher from Rochdale: 28 years in a dye works, now looking for what comes next.

signals.text: The dye works closed at the end of August and I'm looking for work where my colour knowledge counts for something.
I've applied for lab technician and paint or finishing company jobs, and I'd like to hear from anyone in coatings, pigments or textile finishing who is hiring or knows who is.
I'm open to short fixed-term lab work within reach of the Manchester tram line.
I have about 400 shade recipes in a battered notebook and nowhere to put them to use.
I'm sorting a first-year set of dyed swatch cards by hue and would like someone to see them who understands what they are.
My daughter says I should write down or film what I know about colour, but I don't know where to start and I'm not good with computers.
I keep getting asked to translate 'colour matching' into CV language and it comes out flat. I'd like help describing what I actually do.
A lot of my old workmates are out of work or in unrelated jobs, and I haven't yet replied to some who got in touch.
My wife and I are weighing up moving to the coast, and I haven't decided.
I'm getting back into my allotment this autumn: digging, garlic, and working with my hands.
Since the closure I've felt unsure what my knowledge is worth to anyone, and I'd like to be useful again.
I've had rejections that seemed to be about age, and I'd like advice from people who've been through a late-career change.

offers.text: I can match shades by eye to within batch tolerance, and the spectrophotometer agreed with my results. I've done this on wool, polyester, cotton and blends.
I know dye chemistry in practice: reactive, disperse and acid dyes, mordants, pH control, liquor ratios and fixing agents. I can troubleshoot why a dyeing went wrong.
I have recipes for about 400 shades that the works ran regularly, and I can explain how they were built and adjusted.
I have a set of dyed swatch cards from the early years of a working dye house, which could be useful for teaching, exhibitions or archives.
I know people across the north west textile trade, mostly retired or laid off, and can point you to the right one for a question.
I can judge colour by eye in a north-facing window and can give a second opinion on a shade, a paint chart or a fabric match.
I can explain colour and dyeing to beginners, patiently and from practice.
I have time available now, and I can help on a short project or consultation.

catchers.hypo: I run a small craft dye studio or a textile restoration business. My dye batches won't match from one run to the next and I don't have an expert to ask.
catchers.can: Dennis can diagnose the likely causes (pH, liquor ratio, fixing, dye class) and talk you through a matching process. This could be a paid consultation.
catchers.confirm: Is your problem consistency or accuracy when dyeing fibre with reactive, disperse or acid dyes, rather than printing or digital colour?

catchers.hypo: I'm a paint or coatings company in the north west with a fixed-term lab vacancy and I'd take someone with real colour-matching experience over a recent graduate.
catchers.can: Dennis could apply for or fill a lab assistant role, since he has 28 years of hands-on colour matching and a lab background. He needs somewhere reachable by tram or a short commute.
catchers.confirm: Is the role reachable from Rochdale or Manchester without relocating, and does it involve actual colour matching or shade work?

catchers.hypo: I'm making a video series, a podcast or a book about vanishing industrial trades in Lancashire and Yorkshire. I'm looking for someone who can describe the craft first-hand.
catchers.can: Dennis can describe colour matching and dyeing from experience. His daughter Hannah, who lives in Leeds and has been encouraging him to share what he knows, could help with recording.
catchers.confirm: Would you be recording a conversation and handling the editing and publishing yourself, so he wouldn't need to work the technology?

catchers.hypo: I was made redundant after decades in a mill or factory and I don't know how to describe my skills or start again. Has anyone been through this?
catchers.can: Dennis can talk with someone in the same position about how it feels and what he's tried. His brother-in-law Tom and ex-colleagues also keep each other company over a pint or a match.
catchers.confirm: Are you after peer company and practical tips from another worker, rather than counselling or formal career services?

catchers.hypo: I teach textiles or design at a college or community class. I'd like someone who has worked at an industrial dye house to show students real swatches and explain how shade matching is done.
catchers.can: Dennis can show his early swatch cards and recipe notebooks and explain the process in person. This would be a one-off or occasional session.
catchers.confirm: Could the session be in person, within travel distance of Rochdale, and for a small group rather than a lecture hall?

catchers.hypo: I'm a former dye-house worker who's now driving a bus, working in a shop or out of work. I miss the trade and wondered if anyone wanted to share stories or start something together.
catchers.can: Dennis has a network of ex-colleagues and could put you in touch with others in the same position. An informal group or meet-up might form around the swatch cards.
catchers.confirm: Did you work in the north west textile trade, in dyeing or finishing?

catchers.hypo: I live in Southport or on the Lancashire coast and know what it's like to move there from a Greater Manchester town. I'd be glad to tell someone about it.
catchers.can: Dennis's wife Carol is looking at a flat in Southport, and they have a viewing planned. A local could give her honest information about the area.
catchers.confirm: Do you live in Southport itself, and are you happy to answer practical questions about daily life there?

catchers.hypo: I'm an artist, dyer or hobbyist who wants help getting a particular shade right, such as a heritage navy, a school-uniform colour or a faded vintage tone.
catchers.can: Dennis can look at a sample, identify which dye classes are likely and suggest a recipe starting point.
catchers.confirm: Do you have a physical sample or swatch that he could look at, or at least a photograph with lighting information?

forbids.text: I'm not comfortable with computers beyond email and Facebook, so I can't do work that needs complicated software.
I don't want to move away from Rochdale for work, and a commute should be on the tram or a short drive.
I won't talk about my savings, redundancy money or health with strangers.
I'm not a performer, so I'd want any filming kept low-key and in my own words.
I don't want to give away my recipes for free to a company that will profit from them.

projects.name: Dye-house colour archive
projects.text: Preserve and share a set of first-year swatch cards and a notebook of about 400 shade recipes from a closed north west dye works, and record how shades were matched by eye.
roles_needed: colour scientist for comparison with spectrophotometer data

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll say that I was the senior colour matcher, describe my dye-chemistry knowledge and recipe notebook, and name the kinds of work I'm after and can reach.
policy.t2: Once I trust you, I'll talk about how it feels to be out of work and about our family conversation about moving to the coast.
policy.never: Redundancy payout, savings and medical details.
